Job Type

Full-time

Description

At STRIDE Community Health Center, we’re dedicated to more than just providing healthcare, we’re committed to making a lasting impact on the lives of our patients and the communities we serve. As one of Colorado’s largest Federally Qualified Health Centers, we provide comprehensive services—including primary care, dental, pharmacy, behavioral health, health education, and outreach—to individuals and families throughout the Denver Metro area.

With over 35 years of serving our community, our growing team is at the heart of this mission. We believe healthcare is about more than treating illness; it's about fostering wellness and addressing the unique needs of every person, ensuring that no one is left behind. If you’re passionate about making a meaningful difference, thrive in a collaborative environment, and are ready for a career that transforms lives, including your own, STRIDE is the place for you.

Work Schedule

Monday - Friday, 7:00 AM - 5:30 PM

Location
: Wheat Ridge Clinic

Hybrid Schedule (Colorado Residents Only):
3 days onsite and 2 days remote per week. Full-time onsite attendance is required during training until completion.

General Purpose:
As a vital member of the care team, Care Coordinators support the organization’s quality and value-based care efforts through coordination of internal and external services, referral management, and basic health education interventions.

Essential Duties/Position Responsibilities

Coordinates internal and external services for patients in collaboration with the care team.
Utilizes evidence-based screening tools to identify and document social determinants of health (SDH) and health-related social needs (HRSN) and provides resources and referrals to internal and external partners best equipped to address identified barriers.
Knows and maintains the database of community resources available to STRIDE’s patient population.
Documents and communicates in a “closed loop” fashion with both patient and care team from initial interaction to closure of the episode or completion of goals.
Conducts patient interaction(s) with respect, collaboration, and confidentiality utilizing basic principles of motivational interviewing when appropriate.
Provides basic health education using evidence-based educational resources from nationally recognized sources or the Electronic Health Record and refers patients to appropriate internal or external resources for further education and support when indicated.
Manages internal and external referrals in accordance with organization policies, procedures, and standards including maintenance of the referral partner database, referral processing, follow-up with external agencies and providers to “close the loop”, retrieving and indexing reports.
Contributes to population health efforts including targeted outreach and scheduling of patients based on specific criteria such as the presence of a chronic condition, wellness visit due, preventative health needs, recent emergency department or hospital visit, or at provider/organization request.
Follows departmental standard workflows.
Supports quality improvement activities including those informed by external partners, payors, accreditors, and regulators as assigned.
Completes all other duties as assigned.

Requirements

STRIDE Values

Community: All are welcome at STRIDE - our patients are the center of our work.
Trust: Our patients feel safe, empowered, and supported.
Value: We respond to patients' needs by providing effective, affordable care.
Compassion: We treat patients with kindness, empathy, and dignity.

Education And Experience

Required: High school diploma or GED.
Required: Active BLS certification.
At least 1 year of direct or indirect support of patient care or related experience.
At least 1 year of experience in a community health or Federally Qualified Health Center setting is preferred.

Knowledge, Skills And Abilities

Additional language proficiency highly desired.
Ability to interact positively and build rapport with patients, coworkers and/or external contacts.
Ability to respond to the needs and concerns of the full range of STRIDE’s diverse patient population effectively and sensitively.
Ability to handle sensitive information ethically and responsibly.
Ability to protect the confidentiality of patient, employee, and business information.
Ability to discern information from others in a variety of formats and communicate information to others in a manner that helps them understand instruction.
Ability to work independently in a manner that ensures accuracy and efficiency.
Ability to demonstrate empathy with potential cultural and diversity dynamics.
Ability to utilize advanced customer service skills, including the ability to diffuse upset patients.

Miscellaneous Requirements

COVID-19 Vaccination
Annual Influenza Vaccination

At STRIDE Community Health Center, we value a strong and collaborative work environment. To ensure a successful integration into our team, we implement a 90-day probationary period for all new employees. This timeframe is designed to evaluate performance and assess cultural alignment within our organization. It offers both the employee and the employer the opportunity to determine if the role is a mutual fit, promoting long-term success and satisfaction in your career with us. Join our dedicated team and contribute to our mission of providing quality health care to our community!

We offer a competitive hourly range of $20.67 - $24.03
, depending on your experience.

This range reflects STRIDE’s good faith estimate of potential compensation at the time of posting. The final salary for the selected candidate will be determined based on several factors, including experience, education, budget, internal equity, specialty, and training.

Why STRIDE?

Benefits

Join us for a fulfilling career with a comprehensive full-time benefits package that promotes professional growth, well-being, and financial security, including:

Medical, dental, and vision coverage
Paid time off (PTO) and holidays
Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA), including dependent care options
401(k) with matching
Work-life balance
NHSC Loan Repayment
Tuition reimbursement and/or Continuing Medical Education (CME)
No nights, weekends, or major holidays
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)
Employee Discounts on top attractions, hotels, more

STRIDE conducts background checks, including criminal history, education, license and certification.

STRIDE is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to any characteristic protected by law.

STRIDE complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act, providing reasonable accommodations as needed.

Health And Safety Commitment

To ensure the safety of our patients, staff, and communities, all new hires at STRIDE must receive an annual flu shot or provide an exemption, as well as undergo tuberculosis screening and testing.

Applicants will be considered until the position is filled.

Function/Duties of Position

The Department of Psychiatry within the Adult Psychiatry Outpatient Clinic is recruting for a Care Coordinator 2.

This is a clinical support role that is vital in supporting the work of the clinical support staff and providers, consisting of students and learners, residents, and fellows, within the Adult Psychiatry Outpatient Clinic. This individual will independently perform a variety of clinical administrative and technical duties. The Care Coordinator performs activities that are system-focused, ensuring the care is seamless across providers and the care continuum. Care coordination is the task of bridging gaps between facilites, specialists, labs, community resources, and primary care. The Care Coordinator works with the providers to provide clinical support with order entry, medication refills, medication prior authorizations, non-nursing support and education to the patient and family member.

The Care Coordinator reviews patient records and referrals in order to provide coordination of the patient needs prior-to, during the clinic visit, and through the episode of treatment. The care coordinator takes direction from providers, but must use independent judgement within their scope in implementation of those directions. The Care Coordinator will also work with the PAS to provide seamless scheduling, follow up, and communication with patients as appropriate. The care coordinator helps to build and maintain good working relationships with the internal institutional departments as well as external stake holders that provide services to the Adult Psychiatry Outpatient Clinic.

Required Qualifications

Three years’ experience in a hospital or hospital based clinic setting, AND

High School diploma or equivalent, AND

Current BLS certification at hire, AND

One Of The Following Four

Completion of a nationally recognized accredited medical assistant training program, including a practicum (externship) of at least 160 hours, OR
Successful completion of a formal medical services training program of the United States Armed Forces, OR
Current Oregon Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) license (basic or advance) and national EMT registration with the National Registry of Emergency Medical Technicians (NREMT), OR
Current Oregon Practical Nurse License

Job Summary

The Social Worker provides services to patient, family members and/or significant others to help deal with adjustment to illness problems, understanding and accepting diagnoses, prognoses or treatment of new or recurrent disease. Provides counseling and intervention as required for cases of suspected abuse or neglect and also in cases for adoption.

The Social Worker will work closely with the RN Case Manager in implementing safe and appropriate discharge plans and is the primary person responsible for coordination of complex discharge planning including placement.

PERFORMANCE DUTIES

Uses and develops the social work process of assessment, planning, implementation and evaluation.
Collects and assesses data related to individual health care needs including: past medical history, current health status and treatment, necessity/appropriateness for services and setting and follow-up needed to meet needs.
Provides counseling to enable patient/family members and/or significant others to utilize resources and strength to make necessary adjustments due to illness, its impact and changes to be anticipated.
Is an active participant in multidisciplinary rounds.
Communicates daily with RN Case Managers and RN’s on their assigned unit to case find appropriate referrals.
Identifies the need for and convenes family meetings to provide clarity to the patient’s status that result in informed decision making.
Formulates discharge plans by collaborating with the patient/family, healthcare team members and outside agencies. Acts as resources to provide discharge planning for complex cases. These may include new oncology diagnoses, patients with difficult family dynamics, hospice patients, patients facing end of life issues, placement issues such as ECF or Rehab and other patients to meet the need of the case management team.
Is familiar with the legal requirements regarding reporting alleged child and/or adult neglect or abuse. Assesses situations to determine if report needs to be made to either Children’s Protective Services or Adult Protective Services. Coordinates with the physician, nurse manager and case manager to implement a safe plan of care for child if there are concerns regarding abuse/neglect. Coordinates with the physician, nurse manager and case manager to implement a safe plan of care for an adult. Coordinates with the domestic violence service agency to plan counseling service and/or a shelter placement, if necessary.
Documents in patient’s electronic data base ongoing communication with all individuals responsible for the continuum of care or regulatory issues.
Demonstrates the ability to use the various computer programs required.
Conducts support/education groups to assist in adjustment process. As appropriate, may have the option to facilitate either a time limited or ongoing group process to help family members cope with illness, as time permits.
Handles community calls and visits.
Provides on-call coverage for social work interventions on Sundays and Holidays, this may include acting as a resource for directing urgent need for DME or HHC if no Case Manager is available.

Other Duties

Develops and maintains positive, effective communication skills in all interactions
Analyzes and applies appropriate communication style for each situation
Participates in team meetings daily
Participates in the educational process of various co-workers, orientees and other departments as related to Social Work functions.
Demonstrates awareness of and adherence to safety and legal requirements established at hospital and departmental levels
Assists in the planning and implementation of departmental based quality management and disaster response activities
Compliant with HIPPA standards
Accepts accountability and responsibility for own professional growth and development
Promotes an environment that allows for positive, effective areas of practice for all “customers” of Outcomes Management
Remains current on trends in own practice and in areas that involve the department and facility
Maintains current, active status in profession and meets continuing education standards set by the department and/or facility Serves on committees, task forces and focus or work groups on a voluntary and/or appointed basis at the staff/department level

jobs.description:
A LITTLE ABOUT US & WHY WE’RE HIRING

After ten and a half years of growing Striving for Synergy and serving the Toronto community, I am incredibly proud of the psychotherapy practice and team we have built — and we are excited to be growing again.

Striving for Synergy is a therapist-founded private psychotherapy practice specializing in complex trauma, OCD, and attachment-related concerns. Trauma work is at the heart of much of what we do, including attachment and developmental trauma, relational and sexual trauma, PTSD, and complex trauma. OCD and anxiety disorders are also established areas of clinical specialization within our practice.

Over the years, we have built a strong reputation within the Toronto community and among our referral partners for thoughtful, highly specialized clinical care.
As the owner and Clinical Director, maintaining that standard of care is incredibly important to me. We are not looking to simply fill a position. We are looking for the right clinician to join our team, and we are more than willing to wait for that person.

We currently have a significant number of referrals waiting in the wings, particularly for in-person EMDR therapy and couples therapy.

Our office is located at 1849 Yonge Street, directly across from Davisville Station.

THIS IS ACTUALLY A TEAM

When we say team, we genuinely mean it.

We are not simply a collection of independent practitioners who happen to share an office, website, and referral source. We know one another. We consult with one another. We support one another. We laugh and celebrate together, and many genuine friendships have grown within our practice.
You will find us at holiday parties, summer BBQs, dinners, brunches, coffee dates, patio drinks, pedal pubs, team outings, birthdays, and other celebrations. None of this is obligatory, of course, but the connection behind it is a very real part of our culture.

We also care about the person behind the therapist. We care about your wellbeing, your family and life outside of work, your career, and the clinician you want to become.

Therapists do incredibly meaningful work, but it can also be heavy work. We do not believe you should have to do it in isolation. If you want the autonomy of private practice without feeling like you are practicing alone, you may feel very at home here.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for an experienced Registered Psychotherapist, Registered Social Worker, or Psychologist with a strong clinical foundation, thoughtful clinical judgment, and confidence working with complex cases. For this position, our priorities are trauma and attachment therapy, in-person EMDR therapy, couples therapy, and sex therapy.

TRAUMA, ATTACHMENT & EMDR

Formal training in EMDR is required. Training and experience in Internal Family Systems (IFS) is highly recommended. We are looking for someone with meaningful experience working with complex trauma and attachment-related concerns, including developmental trauma, sexual trauma, relational trauma, PTSD, and dissociation. We currently have clients specifically seeking in-person EMDR therapy, so the successful clinician must be comfortable and experienced providing EMDR in person at our Midtown Toronto office.

COUPLES THERAPY

We are specifically looking for an experienced couples therapist who genuinely enjoys couples work, has formal postgraduate training in couples therapy, and feels confident working with relational complexity. Many of our couples referrals involve attachment injuries, trauma histories, betrayal, intimacy and sexual concerns, communication difficulties, conflict, and longstanding patterns of disconnection.

Gottman Method Couples Therapy training is strongly preferred. Clinicians currently completing Gottman training are also encouraged to apply. Additional formal training in established couples and relationship therapy approaches is highly valued.
We currently have couples therapy referrals waiting to be matched with the right therapist.

SEX THERAPY

Formal training in sex therapy is required.
We are looking for a clinician who is comfortable and clinically competent supporting clients with concerns related to sexuality, sexual wellbeing, intimacy, desire, sexual functioning, and relationships.

WHAT WE OFFER

This independent contractor position is designed for a fully registered clinician who wants the autonomy of private practice without having to independently build and manage all of the infrastructure behind it.

Our turn-key practice model includes:
• A steady flow of aligned referrals
• Scheduling and booking support
• Billing and invoicing
• Intake and consultation calls
• Client follow-up and rebooking
• Referral matching and caseload development
• Secure EMR and client management software
• Online booking and secure virtual therapy
• Professional clinic email and client portal
• Established marketing and multiple consistent referral streams
• Monthly individual and/or peer clinical consultation
• Opportunities for workshops, community education, supervision, mentorship, and leadership
• A genuinely collaborative clinical team

You do not need to pay for an EMR, figure out private practice marketing, chase invoices, or manage intake inquiries. You get to focus on being an excellent therapist.

COMPENSATION

We offer a competitive flat rate based on clinical training and experience.
Our flat-rate model provides predictability and transparency while also protecting clinicians when the practice offers sliding-scale or reduced-fee services. In those circumstances, the practice absorbs the financial difference rather than passing the reduction along to the therapist.
We believe client accessibility should not come at the expense of clinician sustainability.

IN-PERSON CASELOAD & AVAILABILITY

This position requires a minimum of 15 in-person client hours per week at our Midtown Toronto office.
Virtual client hours may be offered in addition to those 15 hours, with plenty of opportunity to grow your caseload if desired and clinically sustainable.
The successful clinician must be available for at least two in-person shifts per week, including at least one evening or weekend shift.
Current office availability:
• Monday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
• Tuesday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
• Wednesday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
• Thursday: 8:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m.
• Friday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
• Saturday: after 12:00 p.m.
• Sunday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

We want our clinicians to have thriving practices, but we also care about sustainability and life outside of work.

YOU MIGHT BE A GREAT FIT IF...

Beyond clinical experience, we are looking for someone who is reflective, ethical, warm, grounded, reliable, and genuinely collaborative.
You are curious and committed to continued learning. You are comfortable seeking consultation when a case is complicated and equally willing to share your knowledge with colleagues.
Most importantly, you want to be part of a team. You value the autonomy of private practice, but you do not want to practice in isolation.

REQUIREMENTS

Applicants must:
• Be fully registered and in good standing as an RP with CRPO, MSW/RSW with OCSWSSW, or Psychologist with CPBAO
• Be authorized to perform the controlled act of psychotherapy in Ontario, where applicable
• Have formal EMDR training
• Have meaningful experience working with complex trauma and attachment-related concerns
• Have formal postgraduate couples therapy training and demonstrated experience as a couples therapist
• Ideally have completed Gottman Method Couples Therapy training or currently be enrolled in Gottman training
• Have formal training in sex therapy
• Commit to a minimum of 15 in-person client hours per week
• Be available for at least two in-person shifts per week, including at least one evening or weekend shift
• Reside in Ontario and within reasonable commuting distance of Midtown Toronto
• Maintain professional liability insurance with a minimum of $2 million in coverage
• Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation in accordance with regulatory standards
• Demonstrate a commitment to ongoing consultation, training, and professional development
Training and experience in IFS is highly recommended, particularly given the complex trauma and attachment presentations commonly seen within our practice.

We know this is a specific list. That is intentional.

We are fortunate to have an established practice, an incredible team, strong referral relationships, and clients already waiting for specialized services. We are prepared to take our time finding someone whose clinical experience, values, personality, and professional goals genuinely align with Striving for Synergy.

HOW TO APPLY

If you have read this far and thought, “This sounds like the kind of team I would love to be part of,” we would genuinely love to hear from you.

Please email hello@strivingforsynergy.com with:
• Your CV/resume
• A cover letter telling us about you, your clinical approach, specialized training, and why you are interested in joining Striving for Synergy
• Your current in-person availability and ideal working hours

Both a CV and cover letter are required for an application to be considered. We will contact applicants whose experience, training, clinical interests, and approach appear to align with what we are looking for.

EQUITY, INCLUSION & BELONGING

Striving for Synergy is committed to creating a practice where clients and clinicians from diverse backgrounds, identities, cultures, relationships, and lived experiences feel welcomed, affirmed, and respected. We strongly encourage applications from clinicians with diverse lived experiences and perspectives.

new_jobs.description:
A LITTLE ABOUT US & WHY WE’RE HIRING

After ten and a half years of growing Striving for Synergy and serving the Toronto community, I am incredibly proud of the psychotherapy practice and team we have built — and we are excited to be growing again.

Striving for Synergy is a therapist-founded private psychotherapy practice specializing in complex trauma, OCD, and attachment-related concerns. Trauma work is at the heart of much of what we do, including attachment and developmental trauma, relational and sexual trauma, PTSD, and complex trauma. OCD and anxiety disorders are also established areas of clinical specialization within our practice.

Over the years, we have built a strong reputation within the Toronto community and among our referral partners for thoughtful, highly specialized clinical care.
As the owner and Clinical Director, maintaining that standard of care is incredibly important to me. We are not looking to simply fill a position. We are looking for the right clinician to join our team, and we are more than willing to wait for that person.

We currently have a significant number of referrals waiting in the wings, particularly for in-person EMDR therapy and couples therapy.

Our office is located at 1849 Yonge Street, directly across from Davisville Station.

THIS IS ACTUALLY A TEAM

When we say team, we genuinely mean it.

We are not simply a collection of independent practitioners who happen to share an office, website, and referral source. We know one another. We consult with one another. We support one another. We laugh and celebrate together, and many genuine friendships have grown within our practice.
You will find us at holiday parties, summer BBQs, dinners, brunches, coffee dates, patio drinks, pedal pubs, team outings, birthdays, and other celebrations. None of this is obligatory, of course, but the connection behind it is a very real part of our culture.

We also care about the person behind the therapist. We care about your wellbeing, your family and life outside of work, your career, and the clinician you want to become.

Therapists do incredibly meaningful work, but it can also be heavy work. We do not believe you should have to do it in isolation. If you want the autonomy of private practice without feeling like you are practicing alone, you may feel very at home here.

WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR

We are looking for an experienced Registered Psychotherapist, Registered Social Worker, or Psychologist with a strong clinical foundation, thoughtful clinical judgment, and confidence working with complex cases. For this position, our priorities are trauma and attachment therapy, in-person EMDR therapy, couples therapy, and sex therapy.

TRAUMA, ATTACHMENT & EMDR

Formal training in EMDR is required. Training and experience in Internal Family Systems (IFS) is highly recommended. We are looking for someone with meaningful experience working with complex trauma and attachment-related concerns, including developmental trauma, sexual trauma, relational trauma, PTSD, and dissociation. We currently have clients specifically seeking in-person EMDR therapy, so the successful clinician must be comfortable and experienced providing EMDR in person at our Midtown Toronto office.

COUPLES THERAPY

We are specifically looking for an experienced couples therapist who genuinely enjoys couples work, has formal postgraduate training in couples therapy, and feels confident working with relational complexity. Many of our couples referrals involve attachment injuries, trauma histories, betrayal, intimacy and sexual concerns, communication difficulties, conflict, and longstanding patterns of disconnection.

Gottman Method Couples Therapy training is strongly preferred. Clinicians currently completing Gottman training are also encouraged to apply. Additional formal training in established couples and relationship therapy approaches is highly valued.
We currently have couples therapy referrals waiting to be matched with the right therapist.

SEX THERAPY

Formal training in sex therapy is required.
We are looking for a clinician who is comfortable and clinically competent supporting clients with concerns related to sexuality, sexual wellbeing, intimacy, desire, sexual functioning, and relationships.

WHAT WE OFFER

This independent contractor position is designed for a fully registered clinician who wants the autonomy of private practice without having to independently build and manage all of the infrastructure behind it.

Our turn-key practice model includes:
• A steady flow of aligned referrals
• Scheduling and booking support
• Billing and invoicing
• Intake and consultation calls
• Client follow-up and rebooking
• Referral matching and caseload development
• Secure EMR and client management software
• Online booking and secure virtual therapy
• Professional clinic email and client portal
• Established marketing and multiple consistent referral streams
• Monthly individual and/or peer clinical consultation
• Opportunities for workshops, community education, supervision, mentorship, and leadership
• A genuinely collaborative clinical team

You do not need to pay for an EMR, figure out private practice marketing, chase invoices, or manage intake inquiries. You get to focus on being an excellent therapist.

COMPENSATION

We offer a competitive flat rate based on clinical training and experience.
Our flat-rate model provides predictability and transparency while also protecting clinicians when the practice offers sliding-scale or reduced-fee services. In those circumstances, the practice absorbs the financial difference rather than passing the reduction along to the therapist.
We believe client accessibility should not come at the expense of clinician sustainability.

IN-PERSON CASELOAD & AVAILABILITY

This position requires a minimum of 15 in-person client hours per week at our Midtown Toronto office.
Virtual client hours may be offered in addition to those 15 hours, with plenty of opportunity to grow your caseload if desired and clinically sustainable.
The successful clinician must be available for at least two in-person shifts per week, including at least one evening or weekend shift.
Current office availability:
• Monday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
• Tuesday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
• Wednesday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
• Thursday: 8:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m.
• Friday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.
• Saturday: after 12:00 p.m.
• Sunday: 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.

We want our clinicians to have thriving practices, but we also care about sustainability and life outside of work.

YOU MIGHT BE A GREAT FIT IF...

Beyond clinical experience, we are looking for someone who is reflective, ethical, warm, grounded, reliable, and genuinely collaborative.
You are curious and committed to continued learning. You are comfortable seeking consultation when a case is complicated and equally willing to share your knowledge with colleagues.
Most importantly, you want to be part of a team. You value the autonomy of private practice, but you do not want to practice in isolation.

REQUIREMENTS

Applicants must:
• Be fully registered and in good standing as an RP with CRPO, MSW/RSW with OCSWSSW, or Psychologist with CPBAO
• Be authorized to perform the controlled act of psychotherapy in Ontario, where applicable
• Have formal EMDR training
• Have meaningful experience working with complex trauma and attachment-related concerns
• Have formal postgraduate couples therapy training and demonstrated experience as a couples therapist
• Ideally have completed Gottman Method Couples Therapy training or currently be enrolled in Gottman training
• Have formal training in sex therapy
• Commit to a minimum of 15 in-person client hours per week
• Be available for at least two in-person shifts per week, including at least one evening or weekend shift
• Reside in Ontario and within reasonable commuting distance of Midtown Toronto
• Maintain professional liability insurance with a minimum of $2 million in coverage
• Maintain accurate and timely clinical documentation in accordance with regulatory standards
• Demonstrate a commitment to ongoing consultation, training, and professional development
Training and experience in IFS is highly recommended, particularly given the complex trauma and attachment presentations commonly seen within our practice.

We know this is a specific list. That is intentional.

We are fortunate to have an established practice, an incredible team, strong referral relationships, and clients already waiting for specialized services. We are prepared to take our time finding someone whose clinical experience, values, personality, and professional goals genuinely align with Striving for Synergy.

HOW TO APPLY

If you have read this far and thought, “This sounds like the kind of team I would love to be part of,” we would genuinely love to hear from you.

Please email hello@strivingforsynergy.com with:
• Your CV/resume
• A cover letter telling us about you, your clinical approach, specialized training, and why you are interested in joining Striving for Synergy
• Your current in-person availability and ideal working hours

Both a CV and cover letter are required for an application to be considered. We will contact applicants whose experience, training, clinical interests, and approach appear to align with what we are looking for.

EQUITY, INCLUSION & BELONGING

Striving for Synergy is committed to creating a practice where clients and clinicians from diverse backgrounds, identities, cultures, relationships, and lived experiences feel welcomed, affirmed, and respected. We strongly encourage applications from clinicians with diverse lived experiences and perspectives.
